frames.narration: A client works with any Bag: it adds values, removes them and checks the size. Its five checks rely on the contract of the base type, not on any one subclass.
ListBag is the honest subtype. It keeps every item, duplicates included, so the client passes 5 of 5 checks and never needs to know which subtype it was given.
DedupBag reuses ListBag but ignores a value it already holds. After two adds of 5 the size is 1, not 2: the postcondition is weakened, and 3 of 5 checks pass.
PositiveBag rejects values up to zero, which the base type accepts. The client's add(-1) throws: the precondition was strengthened, and 4 of 5 checks pass.
ReadOnlyBag inherits ListBag and throws on every add. All five write checks fail: 0 of 5. The compiler accepted it everywhere a Bag is expected.
The classic version of the same break: a Square that inherits Rectangle and sets both sides in each setter. Width 5, height 4 gives an area of 16 instead of 20, and 1 of 3 checks pass.
The fix is composition: ReadOnlyView holds a list and offers only reading. It is not a Bag, so the writer client is never given one, and the reader client passes 2 of 2.
Substitutability is about behaviour, not types. A type that cannot keep the promises of a base type should not claim to be it: reuse code by holding it, and keep contracts small.
